To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the biodegradation of chlorophenols in soils can be enhanced by inoculating them with Pseudomonas and Stenotrohomonas strains.
the biodegradation of chlorinated compounds in soils can be enhanced by bioaugmentation with Pseudomonas strains.
the biodegradation of aromatic compounds by the introduced strains was accompanied by changes in the structure and functional diversity of soil microorganisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of applying the tested bacterial strains for the bioremediation of soil polluted with chlorophenolic compounds.
the possibility of using the strains CF600 and KB2 in bioremediation processes.
the biodegradation of the aromatic compounds in the soil and the impact of their degradation products on the soil microflora.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of 2.0 g of 4-CP per kg of soil to a single strain of Pseudomonas and Stenotrohomonas resulted in a decrease in the number and diversity of the microorganisms in the soil.

the inoculation of the soil with Pseudomonas and Stenotromphomonas strains and the addition of phenol and benzoic acid as additional carbon sources could improve the degradation of 5, 10, 20, 40 and 100 ppm of 4-chloophenol.

the inoculation of the contaminated soil with Pseudomonas and Stenotro-phomonas strains, in the presence of phenol or sodium benzoate, caused a significant decrease in the rate of 4-CP biodegradation and a change in the functional diversity as well as the structure of the soil microbial community.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bioaugmentation of the soil with CF600 and SB or P was the most effective way for the degradation of 5 mg 4-CP/kg soil.

inoculation of contaminated soil with CF600 and KB2 and the addition of carbon sources such as P and SB can be used as an alternative to the traditional method of bioremediation of contaminated soil with chlorophenol.
bioaugmentation of soil with CF600 and KB2 and the addition of P or SB as carbon source can be a promising strategy for the degradation of chlorophenol in contaminated soils.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the introduction of the CF600 strain into the soil contaminated by 4-CP and additional carbon source can enhance the biodegradation of the aromatic compound and increase the functional and structural microbial diversity.
the inoculation of the soil with CF600 and SB or P was the most effective way to enhance the 4-CP degradation.
the inoculation of the soil with Pseudomonas CF600 and the introduction of additional carbon sources can be an effective method for the bioremediation of 4-CP-contaminated soils.
